result.title: Metamorphic Testing of Learned Spatial Surrogates for Transit Accessibility
result.summary: Transit-network design requires evaluating many candidates, but detailed accessibility calculations are too slow to repeat inside an optimization loop. We therefore train a neural surrogate to approximate them. Given a candidate bus network and fixed information about rail service and nearby opportunities, it predicts the calculated spatial change in accessibility. We compare its predictions with routing-derived targets in geographically held-out regions and test specified qualitative relations under controlled input changes. Reference calculations on constructed networks assess the applicability of relations that have a routing-level counterpart. Models with positive predictive skill can still fail basic connectivity tests. One targeted intervention substantially increases pass rates for two connectivity relations while predictive skill also improves. Average prediction error is therefore insufficient when a learned model becomes an optimization objective. Predictive agreement and controlled behavioral tests should be reported separately.

AI.brief_summary: 该文训练神经代理模型预测候选公交网络带来的可达性空间变化，并在留出区域对比路由计算目标，同时用受控输入扰动下的定性关系（metamorphic 测试）检验模型行为；发现预测精度尚可的模型仍会通不过基本连通性检验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测一致性与受控行为测试分开报告」的评估协议可供核查：或可迁移为对 latent 推理模型的诊断，检验内部状态在视觉或结构扰动下是否仍满足任务必要的关系约束，而非只看答案平均误差。
